its name, as apps and the desk call it
its id in PipeWire, and its media class
time it works each cycle, on average
tags: what is special about it
a sound card, a headset, a mic: something with hardware
a program that plays or records
WirePlumber's plumbing and PipeWire's own clocks
a camera, a screen being shared
Patchcord's own signal meters and cue
a driver clocks it: it works every cycle
ready, but nothing makes it run
asleep: the device is closed, no CPU
it missed a deadline lately: you may hear a crackle
it gives the clock to its group
WirePlumber's own, left off the desk
made by Patchcord: a meter, the cue
you hid its device on the desk
its rate is not the group's: it is resampled
a node, a port or a link: its details
fit the graph to the window
close the legend, then the details
a port has its block's colour; one port is one channel: FL, FR, MONO…
Inputs are on a block's left, outputs on its right: sound flows left to right.
A link takes the colour of the block it comes out of, so you see which way sound goes.
listens only: never keeps a device awake
PipeWire could not connect it (no common format)
the chosen link: a yellow glow behind it
One link carries one channel: a stereo cord on the desk is two links here.
the driver: the device whose clock the group runs on
the rate everything in the group runs at
one cycle: the deadline for all its nodes
DSP load: how much of the cycle the graph takes
the worst cycle's time left: little left means xruns
no driver clocks these now: suspended devices, idle streams
PipeWire's own clocks, when nothing else runs
the chosen node: a yellow glow behind it; its colours stay
a chosen link (with its two ports) or port: glows the same way
what it is linked to stays as it is
